questions.question: GDP calculated at some constant set of prices is called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**real GDP.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Real GDP** is calculated by **adjusting nominal GDP **for** inflation**, which gives a more accurate measure of **economic growth.**
 
• Real GDP is used to compare** economic growth over time**, as it reflects changes in the quantity of **goods and services **produced rather than changes in prices.
 
• **Domestic GDP** is a measure of the value of all goods and services produced within a **country's borders,** regardless of the nationality of the producers.
 
• **Current GDP** refers to the most recent measurement of a** country's GDP,** regardless of the prices used to calculate it.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is calculated using **current prices** and does not account for **inflation, **which can lead to an overestimation of economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP** stands for **Gross Domestic Product** and is a measure of the **total value of goods and services **produced within a country's borders.
 
• **Real GDP** is considered a more accurate measure of economic growth because it adjusts for inflation, which can distort the** value of goods and services produced.**
 
• **Domestic GDP** is often used in conjunction with other measures, such as **Gross National Product (GNP)**, which includes the value of goods and services produced by a country's citizens, regardless of where they are located.
 
• **Current GDP **is useful for** tracking short-term changes **in the economy, but it may not provide an accurate picture of long-term trends.
 
• **Nominal GDP** is often used to compare the** economic size of different countries or regions**, but it can be misleading if prices are not taken into account.

__
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** was the **last Governor General of British India,** serving from** 1947-1948.**
 
• He was appointed to oversee the** transition of India from British rule **to independence and was instrumental in the** partition of India **and the creation of Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Lord Auckland** served as Governor General from **1836-1842**.
 
• **Lord Wellesley** served as Governor General from **1798-1805** and was known for his administrative and military reforms.

questions.question: Which of the following article of Indian constitution is related with “Separation of Judiciary from Executive"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 50.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50** of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall take steps to** separate the judiciary from the executive** in the** public services** of the State.
 
• The purpose of **separating the judiciary from the executive **is to ensure the** independence of the judiciary**, which is crucial for the rule of law and protection of individual rights.
 
• This separation ensures that the **executive does not interfere **with the functioning of the judiciary and that the judiciary is** free to make impartial decisions** without any external influence.
 
• The separation of powers between the judiciary and the executive is a** fundamental principle of the Indian Constitution **and is necessary for the proper functioning of democracy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 40** of the Indian Constitution is related to the** organization of village panchayats.**
 
• **Article 44 **of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall endeavor to secure for the** citizens a uniform civil code **throughout the territory of India.
 
• **Article 46** of the Indian Constitution states that the State shall promote with** special care the educational and economic interests of the weaker sections **of the people and in particular, of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes.

questions.question: The lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ignition temperature.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ignition temperature** is the** minimum temperature** required for a substance to** ignite spontaneously and sustain combustion.**
 
• It is also called the **auto-ignition temperature.**
 
• This temperature is specific to each substance and depends on its **chemical composition, physical state**, and surrounding conditions such as **pressure and concentration of oxygen.**
 
• The ignition temperature is an important safety parameter for **handling and storing flammable substances.**
 
• If the temperature can be kept below the ignition temperature, the substance will** not catch fire.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Melting point** is a physical property of a substance that determines its ability to change from **solid to liquid state.**

 
 
• It is affected by factors such as** pressure, purity, and crystal structure. **
 
 
 
• **Combustion temperature **is a measure of the energy released during the combustion of a substance.
 
 
• It is influenced by factors such as the **chemical composition of the substance, the amount of oxygen present, and the heat transfer rate.**

questions.question: The reproduction process in which only a single parent is involved is called _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**asexual reproduction.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Asexual reproduction** is a type of reproduction in which **offspring are produced by a single parent** without the involvement of **gametes or fertilization.**
 
• In asexual reproduction, the offspring are **genetically identical to the parent,** as there is no genetic recombination or **mixing of genetic material** from two parents.
 
• Examples of asexual reproduction include **binary fission in bacteria, budding in yeast, and fragmentation in starfish.**
 
• Asexual reproduction is advantageous in **stable environments**, as it allows for rapid reproduction and the ability to colonize new habitats quickly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **In vitro fertilization (IVF)** is a type of** assisted reproductive technology **that involves fertilizing an egg with sperm outside of the body and then transferring the resulting embryo into the uterus.

 
 
• IVF is used in cases of **infertility or genetic disorders. **
 
 
 
• **External fertilization** is a type of sexual reproduction that **occurs outside of the body**, such as in aquatic animals like** fish and amphibians.**
 
 
• The **eggs and sperm** are released into the water, where fertilization occurs.
 
 
 
• **Sexual reproduction** involves the** fusion of gametes** from two parents to produce offspring with genetic diversity.
 
 
• This type of reproduction is common in** animals, plants, and some fungi.**
 
• It allows for **genetic variation**, which can be advantageous in changing environments.

questions.question: Which of the following is the ultimate source of energy for all living organisms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sun.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The ultimate source of energy for all living organisms is the** sun.**
 
• The sun provides energy to plants through the process of **photosynthesis. **
 
• Animals then **consume plant**s (or other animals that have consumed plants) to obtain energy. 
 
• This energy is then used for various processes such as** growth, reproduction, and movement. **
 
• Without the sun,** life on Earth** would not be possible.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soil:** While soil does provide nutrients and water to plants, it is **not** the ultimate source of energy for living organisms.
 
• **Water:** Water is essential for life, but it is** not** a direct source of energy.
 
• **Air:** While oxygen is required for respiration, it is **not** the ultimate source of energy.

questions.question: Which bill led to people staging a widespread protest in Delhi, Haryana, and Punjab in September 2020?

• These bills aimed to reform the **agricultural sector of India **by providing freedom to farmers to sell their produce outside the **Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) mandis.**
 
• The Farmers Bill led to widespread protests in **Delhi, Haryana, and Punjab**, as the farmers believed that the bills would lead to the** dismantling of the APMC mandis,** which would result in them not getting the **Minimum Support Price (MSP) **for their crops.

• **Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Bill, 2019,** was passed by the Indian Parliament in November 2019.

questions.question: The Mughals were descendants of ______ from their father’s side.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Timur.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Mughals** were a dynasty that ruled India from the early **16th to mid-19th century,** and their founder Babur claimed **Timur as his ancestor.**
 
• Babur's father **Umar Sheikh Mirza** was a direct descendant of **Timur's son Miran Shah,** making Babur a Timurid prince. 
 
• Babur's mother **Qutlugh Nigar Khanum** was a descendant of **Genghis Khan, **but this lineage was not emphasized as much as the Timurid connection. ​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Timur (also known as Tamerlane) **was a **Turkic-Mongol conqueror **who founded the **Timurid Empire** in Persia and Central Asia.
 
• **Muhammad Ghori **was a ruler of the **Ghurid dynasty in Afghanistan** and India who defeated** Prithviraj Chauhan** in the Second Battle of Tarain and established **Muslim rule in Delhi. **
 
• **Genghis Khan **was the founder and first emperor of the **Mongol Empire, **which at its height controlled much of Asia and Europe.
 
• **Mahmud of Ghazni **was a Sultan of the **Ghaznavid Empire in Afghanistan **and India who conducted several raids into India and patronized **Persian culture and literature.**

questions.question: The streams of water flowing constantly on the ocean surface in definite directions are called ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is ocean currents. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ocean currents** are the streams of **water flowing constantly** on the ocean surface in **definite directions.**
 
• They are driven by various factors such as **wind, temperature, salinity,** and the** rotation of the earth.**
 
• Ocean currents play a crucial role in regulating the **Earth's climate by distributing heat** from the equator to the poles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Waves** are the** disturbances **that propagate through the **ocean surface** due to wind or other factors.

 
 
• They **do not** have a definite direction of flow.
 
• Waves can be further classified into different types such as** wind waves, swell waves, and tsunami waves** based on their origin and characteristics.
 
 
 
• **Cyclones **are the **low-pressure systems that** form over warm** ocean waters** and are associated with strong winds and heavy rainfall.
 
 
• Cyclones are also known as** hurricanes or typhoons **depending on the region where they occur.
 
• They can cause **significant damage to coastal areas** and marine ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Tides **are the periodic** rise and fall of sea levels** caused by the **gravitational pull of the moon and the su**n. 
 
 
• Tides can be classified into different types such as **spring tides and neap tides** based on their relative positions of the moon, sun, and the Earth.

questions.question: The Yaoshang festival of Manipur is celebrated for ______ days.

__
 
• The **Yaoshang festival of Manipur** is celebrated for **five days.**
 
• It is the biggest and most **popular festival of Manipur, **celebrated in the month of** March.**
 
• The festival marks the **arrival of spring** and is celebrated with great enthusiasm and joy.

questions.question: In countries like Japan, ______ birth rates make the population pyramid ______ at the base.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low, Narrow.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Low birth rates** mean that fewer babies are being born, resulting in a **smaller number of young people **in the population.
 
• This causes the population pyramid to **narrow at the base.**
 
• A narrow population pyramid means that there are **fewer young people in the population** to support the older generation, which can lead to issues with** healthcare, pensions, and the economy.**
 
• Japan is currently facing a** demographic crisis **due to its aging population and **low birth rates**, which is putting a strain on its social welfare systems and economy.
 
• The Japanese government has **implemented various policies **to try to address the issue, such as **promoting immigration** and encouraging women to have more children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **High birth rates, Broad pyramid **would result in a large **number of young people in the population**, which can be beneficial for the economy and social welfare systems in the short term, but can also lead to **overpopulation and strain** on resources in the long term.
 
• **High birth rates, Narrow pyramid **is not a likely scenario, as high birth rates would result in a broad pyramid.
